newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent prices surge higher on NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent prices surge higher on NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel prices surged higher late Tuesday, tracking rising NYMEX futures prices in after-hours trade, traders said.

Midwest spot gasoline prices could get another boost on Wednesday following American Petroleum Institute's estimate of a 5.2 million barrel draw in gasoline stocks in the PADD II region, traders said.
The draw was attributed largely to an outage at BP's 155,000 barrel per day Toledo, Ohio refinery and lower Williams Pipeline system inventories, traders said.

The BP outage did not cause a spike in gasoline differentials last week, and traders said the 5.2 million barrel draw in Midwest stocks could be offset by a late-month shipment into the region from the Gulf coast.

Traders on Wednesday were expected to closely monitor a court hearing in Chicago, where Clark Refining and Marketing Co was battling state regulators seeking to temporarily close its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery.

An explosion and fire rocked the refinery over the weekend and idled a 6,400 barrel per day alkylation unit. Citing a 1995 explosion that killed two workers and a release last year of hydrofluoric acid that floated over a nearby high school, the Illinois Attorney General sought a court order to temporarily shut down the refinery.
Clark refinery manager Bob Martindale said the Blue Island plant is operating safely and called efforts to close the facility "unwarranted and unjustified."

"The Blue Island refinery is safe and has been demonstrating its safety day by day. The nature of Saturday's incident has been exaggerated," he said in a statement released by the independent refining and marketing company.
